summary: Fine-tuning improved both held-out splits in point estimate, but the test-split gain could not be distinguished from noise at n=181. Shipping the off-the-shelf encoder instead.

dev.note: dev was used for model selection, so it is not an unbiased estimate

rationale: MRR@10 delta +0.021, 95% CI [-0.009, +0.051], p=0.16 -- interval spans zero.
Per-query the fine-tune is better on 32 and worse on 25 (sign test p=0.43).
PRD 8.4 allows adoption on point estimates alone, but a health-information product should not ship a model whose claimed benefit is unmeasurable.
The 181-query test split is underpowered for a ~0.02 effect; roughly 4x the queries would be needed. Cross-validation could settle it and is recorded as an open option rather than done.
Off-the-shelf MiniLM already beats BM25 by +0.100 MRR@10 with a CI well clear of zero, so the product loses nothing by declining the fine-tune.
reproduce: python -m src.train  &&  python -m src.evaluate --split test --retriever biencoder --model artifacts/encoder   (then src.evaluate.paired_bootstrap)
